title: Getting the most out of Opus 5.5
brief: Official Claude guide to prompting Opus 5.5, steering long agent runs, and checking results in Claude apps and Claude Code. A practical reference for anyone driving long agent sessions.
details: Anthropic's official operator's guide (claude.dev/blog) for getting the most out of Opus 5.5 in Claude apps and Claude Code. The core advice: hand over the whole task in one message and name the finish line ("done means every endpoint uses the new client and the test suite passes") — Opus 5.5 sustains long multi-hour coding runs better than Opus 5. Delete "think carefully"/"think step by step" lines; it always thinks before replying and removing them speeds up replies without a quality drop. For long runs: put stop-and-ask rules in CLAUDE.md ("keep going when you don't need me; stop only before destructive actions"), fan big audits/migrations out across subagents and check each one's evidence, and keep the task list in a file so it survives context compaction. Checking results: read what it needs from you first, ask it to review diffs/PRs before a human does (early testers found it caught more bugs at lowest effort than Opus 5 at high effort), and ask it to mark anything it couldn't confirm. In Claude apps: attach charts and screenshots directly instead of retyping numbers, hand it long decks to check for self-contradictions, and ask for finished files rather than outlines. Also covers the new safeguards — Opus 5.5 is the first Opus with Fable-level bio/cyber guardrails, so flagged messages switch to an older model (disable in Settings if you want to be asked first) — and the /fast research-preview mode for back-and-forth work.
